analysis: Three changes were examined. (1) NemotronSuperServingPolicy.swift:369 raises maximumEncodedBodyBytes from 8 to 40 MiB, which scales the media/ingress/video ledger charges. I did not see the NemotronSuperLocalImageBinding enforcement code, so whether the binding actually enforces the same bound, and whether the ledger refuses over-budget requests, is unverified. The finding above is low severity and covers only consumer-driven memory reservation. (2) NemotronSuperRequestPlan.swift:87 removes the refusal of JSON response_format combined with tools. validateWireControls still rejects logprobs, logit_bias, prompt_cache_key, n>1, minP, and custom parsers. ToolChoicePromptPolicy.prepare and tool schema validation still run, and the response-format instruction is inserted by preparedRequest. No security boundary is crossed. (3) NemotronSuperLocalOutput.swift:93-98 skips JSON normalization of content when tool calls exist. ToolConstraintValidation.validate(calls, prepared:) still runs before this, and forced choice still yields an empty text. Un-normalized free-form text can accompany tool calls, but this is the consumer's own response and is not a confidentiality issue. A remaining question is whether downstream consumers that expect strictly JSON content with tools have been affected. No change touches encryption, attestation, prefix-cache (T-041) scope or authorization paths. The prefix-cache refusal (prompt_cache_key) is unchanged.

findings.detail: maximumEncodedBodyBytes rises from 8 MiB to 40 MiB (NemotronSuperServingPolicy.swift:369). It feeds encodedHeaderQuote, encodedCopies (UInt64(bodyBytes/4*3)*2 at line 406) and videoChargeBytes (lines 445-448). Every image or video request is therefore charged a much larger ledger reservation, and defaultPrefixBankBytes subtracts mediaChargeBytes(imageCount: 1) (line 293), which shrinks the default prefix bank. A consumer can submit a single large media body, up to the 32 MiB transport cap, and reserve far more shared memory than before. This can starve or refuse concurrent requests and could trigger the Super load/serving admission. The hardcoded pinned constants and the 'video charge stays within one image charge' comment were not re-verified against the new bound. The consumer-controlled memory reservation is availability-relevant (ADV-002), and the effect is bounded by the ledger.
findings.title: Image/video media memory charge quintupled with the 40 MiB body bound; admission and sizing assumptions need review
